{{Vanilla|Bookshelf}}
{{Infobox auto}}
A '''bookshelf''' is a decorative block. Matcha Flavoured makes it cheaper to craft and reduces the books it drops. Since the pack removes the enchanting table, bookshelves are decorative only.

== Obtaining ==
=== Crafting ===
{{Recipes}}
Three books between two rows of wooden slabs make 3 bookshelves.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/recipe/crafting/bookshelf.json}}</ref> The vanilla recipe (six planks and three books for one bookshelf) is removed.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/pack.mcmeta}}</ref>

== Drops ==
A bookshelf broken without {{MCW|Silk Touch}} drops 1 book, where vanilla drops 3. The change matches the cheaper recipe: a bookshelf costs one book to make.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/minecraft/loot_table/blocks/bookshelf.json}}</ref>

== Usage ==
{{Uses}}
Bookshelves are used for decoration, and in the vanilla lectern recipe. Chiseled bookshelves are made from any log in a [[stonecutter]].<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/recipe/stonecutting/chiseled_bookshelf_from_stonecutting_any_logs.json}}</ref>

== Appearance ==
The resource pack retextures bookshelves and chiseled bookshelves.<ref>{{Cite changelog|1.0|quote=Bookshelf and Chiseled Bookshelf Textures}}</ref>

== Trivia ==
* Cheaper bookshelves were a player's suggestion, which the developer took from watching the YouTuber Flow State play the pack: since the enchanting table is removed, bookshelves are less useful and should cost less.<ref>{{Cite video|id=wavOi0ULYpQ|title=How Criticism changed Matcha Flavoured|quote=flow state gave me the idea to make cheap bookshelves. I thought that was a really smart idea because he says he said because enchanting is removed}}</ref>
